({{IPAc-en|ˈ|r|ɑː|ʒ|ɒ|n}}; born February 22, 1986) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. Rondo won two [[List of NBA champions|NBA championships]], was selected four times as an [[NBA All-Star]], earned four [[NBA All-Defensive Team]] honors including two First Team honors, and was named to the [[All-NBA Third Team]] in 2012. Rondo played two years of [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky Wildcats]] before being drafted 21st overall by the [[Phoenix Suns]] in the [[2006 NBA draft]] and immediately traded to the [[Boston Celtics]]. As the team's starting [[point guard]], Rondo helped the Celtics win the [[NBA Finals]] in [[2008 NBA Finals|2008]] and return in [[2010 NBA Finals|2010]]. Rondo was a versatile facilitator, leading the league in assists three times and in steals once; he ranks fourth in Celtics history in assists and third in steals. Rondo has been described as a "stat-sheet stuffer"{{cite web|last=Ramos|first=Kyle|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/blog/rajon-rondo-mr.-triple-double|title=Rajon Rondo: Mr. Triple Double|work=NBA.com|date=November 20, 2015|access-date=April 30, 2018}} as his 32 regular season [[triple-doubles]] rank 16th in NBA history,{{cite web |title=Most Triple Doubles |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/leaders/triple-double-most-times.html |website=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=March 5, 2019}} while his 10 in the playoffs rank sixth.{{cite web|url=http://bkref.com/tiny/ixQ64|title=Rajon Rondo Game Finder – triple-doubles|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=February 27, 2016}}{{cite web |url=https://sportslistoftheday.com/2013/04/21/nba-players-with-the-most-triple-doubles-in-playoff-history/ |title=NBA: Players with the Most Triple-Doubles in Playoff History |last=Getz |first=Vin |date=April 21, 2013 |work=Sports List of the Day |access-date=February 4, 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151121193901/http://sportslistoftheday.com/2013/04/21/nba-players-with-the-most-triple-doubles-in-playoff-history/ |archive-date=November 21, 2015}} He is regarded as one of the Celtics' greatest point guards ever. After {{frac|8|1|2}} seasons with the Celtics, Rondo was traded to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in December 2014. After a tumultuous five-month stint he turned into a [[Journeyman (sports)|journeyman]], joining the [[Sacramento Kings]], [[Chicago Bulls]], [[New Orleans Pelicans]], [[Los Angeles Lakers]] (two stints), [[Atlanta Hawks]], [[Los Angeles Clippers]], and [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] over the next {{frac|7|1|2}} years. He won a second championship in [[2020 NBA Finals|2020]] with the Lakers. ==Early life== Rondo was born on February 22, 1986, in [[Louisville, Kentucky]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/rajon_rondo/bio/ |title=Rajon Rondo Stats, Video, Bio, Profile |access-date=December 18, 2014 |work=NBA.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141221071518/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/rajon_rondo/bio |archive-date=December 21, 2014}} He has three siblings.Springer, Shira, [https://archive.boston.com/sports/basketball/celtics/articles/2009/05/17/no_catching_rondo/?page=2 No catching Rondo] , The Boston Globe, May 17, 2009, accessed July 20, 2009. He had little contact with his father, who left his family when he was seven years old. To support the family, his mother worked the third shift at [[Philip Morris USA]], a tobacco company. Rondo was first interested in [[American football|football]], before his mother steered him towards basketball because she felt that the sport would be less punishing on his skinny frame. After Rondo became serious about basketball, he attended Louisville's [[Eastern High School (Louisville)|Eastern High School]] for three years. During his [[Eleventh grade|junior year]] at Eastern High School, he averaged 27.9 [[point (basketball)|points]], 10.0 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] and 7.5 [[assist (basketball)|assists]] which earned him a spot on the All-State honors and was named the 7th Region Player of the Year. He transferred to Virginia's [[Oak Hill Academy (Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] for his [[Twelfth grade|senior year]] where he averaged 21.0 [[points per game]] (ppg), 3.0 [[rebounds per game]] (rpg) and 12.0 [[assists per game]] (apg) and finished the 2003–04 season with a 38–0 record.{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/highschool/rise/basketball/boys/news/story?id=4145715 | title=Rondo makes name for himself despite being overlooked as recruit, pro prospect | publisher=[[ESPN]] | first=Ronnie |last=Flores | date=May 7, 2009 | access-date=May 9, 2009}} In his [[Twelfth grade|senior year]] at Oak Hill Academy, Rondo broke [[Jeff McInnis]]'s single-season school record of 303 assists, while averaging a [[Double (basketball)|double-double]]. There, he included two efforts of 27 assists and a single-game school record of 31, merely four away from the all-time national record. He also had a 55-point game in [[high-school]], second highest all-time in Oak Hill Academy, surpassed only by Calvin Duncan with 61.{{cite web | url=http://www.oakhillhoops.com/records_stats/highgames.html | title=Individual High Scoring Games | access-date=May 9, 2009 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090504001942/http://www.oakhillhoops.com/records_stats/highgames.html | archive-date=May 4, 2009 | df=mdy-all}} Rondo was named to the [[McDonald's All-American Team]] in 2004 and scored a total of 14 points, 4 assists and 4 rebounds in the all-star game.[http://scouthoops.scout.com/2/235809.html 2004 McDonald's All-American Team] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150101194926/http://scouthoops.scout.com/2/235809.html |date=January 1, 2015}} He also participated in the 2004 [[Jordan Brand Capital Classic]] game, logging 12 points, 5 assists and 4 steals.[http://www.jordanbrandclassic.com/archives/2004-jordan-brand-classic-box-score.html 2004 Jordan Brand Classic Box Score] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121128232333/http://www.jordanbrandclassic.com/archives/2004-jordan-brand-classic-box-score.html |date=November 28, 2012}} Rondo was also named a second-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]]. He ended his career as Oak Hill Academy's all-time assists leader in a single season with 494 assists, surpassing McInnis.{{cite web | url=http://www.oakhillhoops.com/records_stats/individual.html | title=Individual Player Records | access-date=May 9, 2009 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090427034207/http://www.oakhillhoops.com/records_stats/individual.html | archive-date=April 27, 2009 | df=mdy-all}} ==College career== Rondo committed to [[University of Kentucky|Kentucky]] over hometown [[University of Louisville|Louisville]].{{cite news |url=http://www.cincypost.com/2004/12/17/ukhoop12-17-2004.html |title=Rondo plays it low-key |last=Sun |first=Victoria |work=[[The Cincinnati Post]] |date=December 17, 2004 |access-date = March 12, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050404041710/http://www.cincypost.com/2004/12/17/ukhoop12-17-2004.html |archive-date=April 4, 2005}} Rondo, along with [[McDonald's All-American|All-Americans]] [[Joe Crawford (basketball, born 1986)|Joe Crawford]] and [[Randolph Morris]], gave coach [[Tubby Smith]] and Kentucky the top-rated recruiting class for 2004 according to [[Rivals.com]].{{cite web |url=http://rivalshoops.rivals.com/content.asp?SID=910&CID=297763 |title=Rivals.com Top 25 for 2004 |publisher=Rivals.com |access-date=March 12, 2007 |archive-date=April 13, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160413054356/https://rivalshoops.rivals.com/content.asp?SID=910&CID=297763 |url-status=dead}} Rondo led Kentucky to several wins including victories against [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]], [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]] and [[UCF Knights men's basketball|Central Florida]], but Kentucky failed to advance to the Final Four of the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] in either Rondo's freshman or sophomore seasons. He was named to the [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] All-Freshmen Team.{{cite web | url=http://www.secsports.com/index.php?s=&url_channel_id=3&url_article_id=6367&change_well_id=2 | archive-url=https://archive.today/20120909121932/http://www.secsports.com/index.php?s=&url_channel_id=3&url_article_id=6367&change_well_id=2 | url-status=dead | archive-date=September 9, 2012 | title=Kentucky, Tennessee Favored By Media To Win SEC Titles | work=SEC Sports | date=October 27, 2005 | access-date=May 9, 2009}} He set a [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] record for most steals in single-season, with a total of 87 steals in his freshman year and made at least one steal in every game.{{cite web | url=http://www.ukathletics.com/genrel/051104aae.html | title=Kentucky Official Athletic Site – Athletics News | access-date=May 9, 2009 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120303101014/http://www.ukathletics.com/genrel/051104aae.html | archive-date=March 3, 2012 | df=mdy-all}} He finished his freshman year at Kentucky averaging 8.1 points, 2.9 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 2.6 steals."[http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/players/37763 Rajon Rondo – Kentucky Wildcats – College Basketball] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130322232326/http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/players/37763 |date=March 22, 2013}}". [[Rivals.com]], accessed July 13, 2009 In his [[sophomore year]], he had a career-high 12 assists against [[Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball|Ole Miss]], despite playing just 23 minutes, and 25 points against Louisville.{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=290040097| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180626165354/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=290040097| url-status=dead| archive-date=June 26, 2018| title=No. 18 Louisville escapes meltdown on Sosa's 25-footer with 2.8 seconds left| work= [[ESPN]]| date=December 18, 2009 | access-date=May 9, 2009}} Rondo also set another Kentucky record for most rebounds in a game by a guard, with 19 rebounds in an early season loss to [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=253250096 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200205130219/https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=253250096 |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 5, 2020 |title=Hawkeyes stun Kentucky, advance to Guardians final |publisher=ESPN |date=November 21, 2005 |access-date=October 20, 2021}} He was not known for being a shooter, however, going 18–66 from the [[three-point field goal|three-point line]] with a 57.1 percent [[free throw]] average. He averaged 11.2 points, 6.1 rebounds, 4.9 assists and 2.1 steals per game in his sophomore year. Rondo was also named to the U.S. men's national under-21 basketball team, which traveled to [[Argentina]] for the [[2005 FIBA Under-21 World Championship]].{{cite web | url=http://www.usabasketball.com/news.php?news_page=mu21_2005 | title=Fourth FIBA Men's U21 World Championship – 2005 | access-date=May 9, 2009 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100103191101/http://usabasketball.com/news.php?news_page=mu21_2005 | archive-date=January 3, 2010 | df=mdy-all}} He averaged 11.0 points and 4.5 assists in the eight-game tournament, garnering much attention from NBA scouts. The U.S. men's national under-21 basketball team won the gold medal at the Global Games held in [[Texas]] in late July.{{citation needed|date=September 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Boston Celtics (2006–2014)=== ====2006 NBA draft==== Following the 2005–06 NCAA season, Rondo announced he would forgo his final two seasons at Kentucky and enter the NBA draft.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2006/news/story?id=2396657 |title=Kentucky G Rondo to hire agent, test draft prospects |work=ESPN.com |first=Chad |last=Ford |date=April 4, 2006 |access-date = March 12, 2007}} Rondo was drafted 21st overall by the [[Phoenix Suns]] in the [[2006 NBA draft]]. Phoenix then traded him to the [[Boston Celtics]] along with [[Brian Grant]] for the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]' first-round draft pick in the [[2007 NBA draft]] and cash considerations.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/draft-central/press062806-draft-rondo.html |title=Celtics Acquire Draft Rights to Rajon Rondo and Brian Grant |work=NBA.com |access-date = March 12, 2007}} He was the first [[point guard]] to be chosen in the draft.Lexington Herald-Leader (June 29, 2006). Rondo was signed by the Celtics on July 4, 2006.[http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/notes070406-west-point.html West Invites Competition at Point] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160323085732/http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/notes070406-west-point.html |date=March 23, 2016}} ====2006–07 season: Rookie year==== During [[2006–07 NBA season|his rookie season]] in the NBA, Rondo played a supporting role and would split time with [[Sebastian Telfair]] and [[Delonte West]]. Rondo only started in 25 games that season due to his initial backup role to Telfair. He made his NBA regular season debut on November 1, 2006, in a home loss against the [[New Orleans Hornets]].Associated Press. (November 1, 2006). "[https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=261101002 NO/Oklahoma City Hornets vs. Boston Celtics Recap] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160126142753/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=261101002 |date=January 26, 2016}}". While coming off the bench, he managed to score a career-high 23 points against the Toronto Raptors, and record his first career [[Double (basketball)|double-double]] in a road losing effort against the [[Washington Wizards]]."[http://www.nba.com/games/20070120/BOSWAS/boxscore.html NBA.com: Celtics at Wizards Boxscore] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160419054246/http://www.nba.com/games/20070120/BOSWAS/boxscore.html |date=April 19, 2016}}". NBA.com. July 13, 2009. ESPN. Retrieved on July 14, 2009. and a career-high 7 steals against the [[Indiana Pacers]]). As the mid-season approached, his numbers began to increase,{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/rookies/rankings_0607.html | title=Rookie Rankings – 2006–07 | work=[[NBA.com]] | first=John |last=Schuhmann | date=July 1, 2007 | access-date=July 10, 2009}} which earned him an [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] selection.{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/All_Access_Online_Marcus_Williams_All_Rookie_Second_Team.html| title=Marcus Williams named to Al—Rookie second team| work= nba.com| date=May 9, 2007 | access-date=May 9, 2009}} He finished the season with an average of 6.4 ppg and 3.8 apg,[http://www.nba.com/playerfile/rajon_rondo/career_stats.html Rajon Rondo Info Page – Career Stats and Totals] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150111143607/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/rajon_rondo/career_stats.html |date=January 11, 2015}}, nba.com, accessed July 20, 2009. ranking in the top ten in the NBA in steals (128){{cite web | url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/notes/notes050807-rondo-rookie-team.html | title=Rondo Named to NBA All-Rookie Second Team | work=Celtics.com | first=Peter |last=F. Stringer | date=May 8, 2007 | access-date=May 9, 2009}} and also ranking in the top ten among rookies in several other categories, including first in steals, second in assists and sixth in minutes. In the end, however, the Celtics finished the season with a 24–58 win–loss record and failed to qualify for [[2007 NBA playoffs|the playoffs]]. ====2007–08 season: First championship==== [[File:Rajon Rondo.jpg|thumb|right|Rondo in May 2008]] After Telfair and West were traded during the off-season of the [[2007–08 NBA season|2007–08 season]], Rondo secured a spot in the [[starting lineup]], starting in every game. Surrounded by [[All-Stars]] [[Kevin Garnett]], [[Paul Pierce]] and [[Ray Allen]], he quickly became a steady, consistent player.{{cite web | url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/BOS/2008.html| title=2007–08 Boston Celtics Roster and Stats| work= basketball-reference.com| date=August 17, 2008 | access-date=May 9, 2009}} In his 77 games played, he averaged 10.6 points per game (ppg), 5.1 assists per game (apg) and 4.2 rebounds per game (rpg). His role as a playmaker reflected in him leading the team in assists and steals. ESPN. Retrieved on July 18, 2009. Despite his solid rookie year, there was much speculation about Boston needing a veteran point guard.{{cite magazine |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2008/writers/chris_mannix/06/18/rondo.clincher/ |title=Celtics' Rondo responds in clincher |last=Mannix |first=Chris |date=June 18, 2008 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=July 12, 2009 |archive-date=October 25, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121025194046/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2008/writers/chris_mannix/06/18/rondo.clincher/ |url-status=dead}} In March, they signed veteran point guard [[Sam Cassell]] as a [[free agent]] to serve as a backup. The Celtics' best single-season improvement in NBA history earned them the number one seed in the Eastern Conference Playoffs. Following the regular season, Rondo finished in the top five for the [[NBA Most Improved Player Award|NBA Most Improved Player]] voting.{{cite news|url=https://www.nba.com/news/hedo_mip_080428.html |title=Hedo Turkoglu Wins Most Improved Player Award |date=April 28, 2008 |work=NBA.com |access-date=July 13, 2009}} Rondo made his playoff debut on April 20, 2008, against the Atlanta Hawks and finished the game with 15 points, 9 assists and 2 steals. The Celtics closed out the series in seven games, went on to defeat [[Cleveland Cavaliers|Cleveland]] in the next round, and then beat the Pistons in the [[NBA conference finals|Eastern Conference finals]]. In the NBA Finals, facing the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], Rondo recorded two strong performances, including a career-high 16 assists in game 2. In game 3, however, Rondo left the court in the third quarter after rolling his ankle.{{cite news | url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/06/12/sports/basketball/12nba.html | title=Rondo's Injury Adds Uncertainty to Celtics' Backcourt | work=[[Los Angeles Times]] | first=Billy |last=Witz | date=June 12, 2008 | access-date=July 12, 2009}} The ankle injury was considered a "non-factor," and Rondo eventually made his return in game 4.{{cite web | url=http://tucsoncitizen.com/morgue/2008/06/12/88036-celtics-rondo-ankle-injury-won-t-keep-me-out-of-game-4/| title=Celtics' Rondo: Ankle injury won't keep me out of Game 4 | work=tucsoncitizen.com | date=June 12, 2008 | access-date=July 12, 2009}} In game 6, the point guard posted a playoffs career-high six steals as the Celtics defeated the Lakers 4–2, giving Rondo his first NBA [[championship ring]]. After the game Lakers head coach [[Phil Jackson]] called Rondo the "star" of game 6. ====2008–09 season: Breakthrough==== [[File:Rajon Rondo 2008.jpg|thumb|left|Rondo guarding [[Juan Dixon]] in December 2008]] In his [[2008–09 NBA season|third NBA campaign]], the Celtics began the season with the best starting record in [[NBA records|NBA history]] and also set a franchise record with a nineteen-game winning streak.Associated Press (December 25, 2008). The arrest came after he was pulled over for reckless driving. He would be released after posting a $700 bond. Though all of the initial charges he was arrested for were considered to be only misdemeanors, it was later acknowledged that his 2022 legal agreement included a no-contact order which forbade him from keeping a gun. An initial court hearing has been scheduled to be held on February 27, 2024.{{cite news|url=https://www.wdrb.com/news/crime-reports/former-uk-nba-star-rajon-rondo-arrested-on-gun-marijuana-charges-in-indiana/article_f9757e14-bf21-11ee-9138-ef5894810a32.html|title=Former UK, NBA star Rajon Rondo arrested on gun, marijuana charges in Indiana|first=Jason|last=Riley|publisher=WDRB|date=January 30, 2024|access-date=January 30, 2024}} Rondo initially pled not guilty to all charges. The case was postponed for several months, while awaiting the decision of the [[United States Supreme Court]] on [[United States v. Rahimi]], which directly pertained to Rondo's defense on the gun charge. Following the Supreme Court's decision, an August 1, trial date was set for Rondo.
